timeline.body: CIA and MI6 overthrew Prime Minister Mosaddegh after he nationalized Iran's oil, ending Iran's democratic experiment and installing Shah Pahlavi as a Western client ruler.
The Iranian Revolution toppled the Shah and established the Islamic Republic, severing all ties with the United States and Israel in a single stroke.
Iraq invaded Iran with Western and Gulf Arab backing, starting an eight-year war that killed half a million people and poisoned Iran's trust in its neighbors for a generation.
The Tanker War saw 451 attacks on merchant shipping in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, establishing the precedent that Gulf oil transit is a weapon of war.
The Strait of Hormuz is 104 miles long and narrows to just 24 miles between Iran's coast and Oman's Musandam Peninsula.
Roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply passes through its shipping lanes every day — whoever controls the strait holds a hand on the global economy's throat.
Iran's coastline commands the northern shore for the entire length of the passage, giving it geographic leverage that no sanctions regime or military deployment can erase.
Israel and Iran maintained a quiet alliance under the Shah, with intelligence cooperation, arms sales, and shared opposition to Arab nationalist governments.
The Islamic Republic made opposition to Israel a pillar of its foreign policy, funding and arming Hezbollah, Hamas, and Islamic Jihad as an "Axis of Resistance" across the region.
Israel destroyed Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor in Operation Opera, establishing the Begin Doctrine: no state in the region would be permitted to approach nuclear capability.
The JCPOA nuclear deal between Iran and world powers capped enrichment and opened inspections in exchange for sanctions relief, briefly lowering tensions.
The United States withdrew from the JCPOA and reimposed maximum-pressure sanctions, collapsing the diplomatic framework and accelerating Iran's enrichment program.
Decades of shadow war escalated into large-scale armed conflict between Iran and Israel, drawing in proxies, shipping lanes, and now the question of Gulf Arab military involvement.
Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, and Oman formed the Gulf Cooperation Council partly in response to the Iranian Revolution and the Iran-Iraq War raging across the water.
GCC states host the largest concentration of American military bases in the Muslim world, making neutrality between Washington and Tehran structurally impossible.
Yet Iran sits directly across the strait — the UAE's commercial ports are closer to Iranian shores than to Riyadh, and any Gulf war would unfold in their territorial waters.
For decades Gulf monarchies have tried to balance Western security partnerships against the reality that a war with Iran would be fought in their own backyards, not Washington's.
"And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allāh. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing." — Quran 8:61

timeline.body: After September 11, Congress federalized airport screening by creating the Transportation Security Administration, replacing private contractors who had failed to detect the hijackers.
The Homeland Security Act consolidated 22 federal agencies into the new Department of Homeland Security — the largest US government reorganization since 1947.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement launched under DHS, merging customs and immigration enforcement into a single agency with broad domestic arrest powers.
President Reagan fired 11,345 striking air traffic controllers, establishing that essential federal workers could be compelled to serve or be permanently replaced.
A 16-day shutdown furloughed 800,000 federal workers — the first time TSA screeners faced working with no guarantee of timely pay.
The longest shutdown in US history lasted 35 days; TSA agents worked unpaid, sickout rates doubled, and airport security lines stretched for hours nationwide.
The standoff broke only after air traffic controllers refused to work and flights ground to a halt at LaGuardia, proving essential workers held the real leverage.
The Posse Comitatus Act of 1878 bars the military from domestic law enforcement, but DHS agencies like ICE operate as civilian federal police outside its constraints.
Since 1976 the federal government has shut down more than 20 times; Congress guaranteed back pay in 2019, but only retroactively — workers go weeks without income while the standoff plays out.
ICE's airport operations have expanded from immigration checkpoints to broader enforcement actions, increasing its visible armed presence in civilian terminals.
